_comment: Compact source for the irregular-verb dataset. Only SIMPLE tenses are stored — every compound tense is derived by tools/build-verbs.js from the auxiliary + past participle, so compounds cannot drift or be invented. Order of forms is always [io, tu, lui/lei, noi, voi, loro]. Run: node tools/build-verbs.js

irregularity.description: The most irregular verb in Italian. Its forms come from three different Latin verbs (esse, fui, stare), so the stems bear no relation to the infinitive: sono/sei/è, ero, fui, sarò. The past participle 'stato' is borrowed wholesale from stare.

presente.italian: Sono italiano e abito a Roma.
presente.english: I am Italian and I live in Rome.

passato_prossimo.english: Yesterday I went to the seaside.

imperfetto.english: As a child I was very shy.

passato_remoto.english: Dante was a great poet.

futuro_semplice.english: Tomorrow I will be in Milan.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Penso che sia una buona idea.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I think it is a good idea.

condizionale_presente.english: I would be happy to help you.

notes: Auxiliary of itself: 'sono stato', not 'ho stato'.
With essere the past participle agrees with the subject: sono stato / sono stata / siamo stati / siamo state.
The present participle 'ente' survives only inside compounds and is not used as a verb form in modern Italian.
The passato remoto is alive in writing and in southern speech; in the north the passato prossimo replaces it in conversation.

irregularity.description: Four present forms are contracted and written with a silent h (ho, hai, ha, hanno) purely to distinguish them from o, ai, a, anno. The future and conditional drop the theme vowel (avrò, not *averò), and the passato remoto has the strong forms ebbi/ebbe/ebbero.

presente.italian: Ho due sorelle e un fratello.
presente.english: I have two sisters and one brother.

passato_prossimo.italian: Ho avuto la febbre per tre giorni.
passato_prossimo.english: I had a fever for three days.

imperfetto.english: I was very hungry.

passato_remoto.english: He had a brilliant idea.

futuro_semplice.english: Tomorrow I will have more time.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I think he is right.

condizionale_presente.english: I would need some advice.

notes: Auxiliary of itself: 'ho avuto'.
The h is never pronounced; it exists only in writing.
Used for physical sensations and age where English uses 'to be': ho fame, ho sete, ho freddo, ho vent'anni.
Auxiliary for the great majority of transitive verbs in the compound tenses.

irregularity.description: The present and subjunctive present use the suppletive stem 'vad-/va-' from Latin vadere, unrelated to the infinitive; noi and voi keep the regular stem (andiamo, andate). The future and conditional contract to andr-.

presente.english: I go to work by underground.

passato_prossimo.italian: Siamo andati al cinema ieri sera.
passato_prossimo.english: We went to the cinema last night.

imperfetto.english: Every summer we used to go to Sicily.

passato_remoto.english: In 1990 he went to live abroad.

futuro_semplice.english: Next year I will go to Japan.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Voglio che tu vada dal medico.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I want you to go to the doctor.

condizionale_presente.english: I would gladly go, but I can't.

notes: Takes essere, so the participle agrees: sono andato / sono andata / siamo andati / siamo andate.
andare a + infinitive expresses purpose: 'Vado a mangiare' (I'm going to eat).
The imperative tu has two written forms: va' (with apostrophe) and vai; both are standard.
Before pronouns the short imperative doubles the consonant: vacci, vattene.

irregularity.description: A contracted infinitive from Latin facere: the full stem fac- resurfaces throughout (faccio, facevo, facendo, facessi), while the infinitive itself is short. Passato remoto is strong (feci, fece, fecero) and the participle is fatto.

presente.english: I have breakfast at seven.

imperfetto.english: It was very cold that night.

passato_remoto.english: Michelangelo made the David.

futuro_semplice.english: Tomorrow I will do the shopping.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I hope the weather is nice.

condizionale_presente.english: I would do anything to help you.

notes: Weather expressions use fare, not essere or avere: fa freddo, fa caldo, fa bel tempo.
fare + infinitive is causative: 'Faccio riparare la macchina' (I have the car repaired).
Very productive in set phrases: fare colazione, fare la spesa, fare una passeggiata, fare sport.
Before pronouns the short imperative doubles the consonant: fallo, fammi, fatti.

irregularity.description: Regular in the imperfetto but irregular elsewhere: monosyllabic io form (sto), subjunctive in stia, and a strong passato remoto with -tt- (stetti, stette, stettero). Shares its participle 'stato' with essere.

presente.english: How are you? — I'm fine, thanks.

passato_prossimo.italian: Sono stato a casa tutto il giorno.

imperfetto.italian: Stavo per uscire quando hai chiamato.
imperfetto.english: I was about to go out when you called.

passato_remoto.english: He stayed silent for an hour.

futuro_semplice.english: I will stay in Rome for three days.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I hope you are feeling better.

condizionale_presente.english: I would happily stay a bit longer.

imperativo.english: Don't worry, I'll take care of it.

notes: Health and wellbeing use stare, not essere: 'Come stai?', 'Sto male'.
stare + gerundio expresses an action in progress: 'Sto mangiando' (I am eating).
stare per + infinitive means 'to be about to': 'Sto per uscire'.
Shares the participle 'stato' with essere, so 'sono stato' can mean both 'I was' and 'I stayed'.

irregularity.description: Monosyllabic io form (do) and a third person written with an accent (dà) to distinguish it from the preposition da. The passato remoto has two accepted series, diedi/diede/diedero and detti/dette/dettero.

presente.english: I'll give you my number.

passato_prossimo.italian: Mi ha dato un buon consiglio.

imperfetto.english: He always used to give me a hand.

passato_remoto.english: He gave her a gold ring.

futuro_semplice.english: I will give you an answer tomorrow.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Basta che tu mi dia il tuo indirizzo.
congiuntivo_presente.english: It's enough for you to give me your address.

condizionale_presente.english: I would give anything to understand it.

notes: 'dà' (verb) carries an accent; 'da' without it is the preposition 'from/by'.
The detti/dette/dettero series is fully standard but less frequent in writing than diedi/diede/diedero.
Set phrases: dare del tu/del Lei, dare una mano, dare fastidio, dare un esame.
Before pronouns the short imperative doubles the consonant: dammi, dallo, dacci.

irregularity.description: Contracted from Latin dicere: the full stem dic- reappears in most forms (dico, dicevo, dicendo), while voi keeps the short form 'dite'. Strong passato remoto (dissi, disse, dissero) and participle detto.

presente.english: I always tell you the truth.

imperfetto.english: He always used to say the same things.

passato_remoto.italian: Disse di no e se ne andò.
passato_remoto.english: He said no and left.

futuro_semplice.english: I will tell him tomorrow.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Non credo che dica la verità.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't think he is telling the truth.

condizionale_presente.english: I would say yes.

notes: dire is followed by 'che' for reported statements and by 'di' + infinitive for reported orders: 'Dice che viene' vs 'Dice di venire'.
Do not confuse with parlare (to speak) or raccontare (to tell a story).
The imperative 'di'' always takes an apostrophe, never an accent.
Before pronouns the short imperative doubles the consonant: dimmi, dillo, digli.

irregularity.description: The velar stem veng- appears before -o and -ono, and the diphthong ie- in tu/lui (vieni, viene). The future contracts with a double r (verrò) and the passato remoto is strong (venni, venne, vennero).

presente.english: Are you coming with us tonight?

passato_prossimo.english: She came to visit me yesterday.

imperfetto.english: He used to come to school by bike.

passato_remoto.english: He came to us in 1985.

futuro_semplice.english: I will come and pick you up at eight.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I hope he comes too.

condizionale_presente.english: I would gladly come, but I'm working.

notes: Takes essere: sono venuto / sono venuta / siamo venuti / siamo venute.
venire a + infinitive expresses purpose: 'Vengo a prenderti'.
venire also forms the passive in place of essere: 'Il libro viene letto' = the book is (being) read.
The same pattern is followed by all its derivatives: divenire, provenire, avvenire, convenire, intervenire.

irregularity.description: The stressed stem changes u- to e- in the four forms where the stress falls on the stem (esco, esci, esce, escono); noi and voi keep the regular stem. Everything else is regular.

presente.italian: Esco con gli amici il venerdì.
presente.english: I go out with friends on Fridays.

imperfetto.english: I always used to leave the office late.

passato_remoto.english: He went out without saying a word.

futuro_semplice.english: Tonight we will go out for dinner.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Non credo che esca con questo tempo.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't think he'll go out in this weather.

condizionale_presente.english: I would go out, but I'm exhausted.

notes: Takes essere: sono uscito / sono uscita.
Note the spelling: esci is pronounced with the soft sound /ʃ/, no h is added.
riuscire (to succeed, to manage) follows exactly the same pattern: riesco, riesci, riesce, riusciamo, riuscite, riescono.
riuscire a + infinitive = to manage to do something.

irregularity.description: Modal verb with the stem posso/può alternation in the present, a subjunctive in possa, and a contracted future stem potr-. It has no imperative, since one cannot order somebody to be able to.

presente.english: I can't come tonight.

passato_prossimo.italian: Non ho potuto finire il lavoro.

imperfetto.italian: Da bambino non potevo uscire da solo.
imperfetto.english: As a child I couldn't go out alone.

passato_remoto.english: He could not attend the meeting.

futuro_semplice.english: Tomorrow I will be able to help you.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I think he can make it.

condizionale_presente.english: Could you speak more slowly?

notes: Modal verb: it is followed directly by the infinitive, with no preposition — 'posso venire', never *'posso di venire'.
In the compound tenses the auxiliary is normally that of the following infinitive: 'ho potuto lavorare' but 'sono potuto andare'. Spoken Italian widely tolerates avere in both cases.
The conditional 'potresti / potrebbe' is the standard polite way to make a request.
The passato remoto series potetti/potette/potettero is correct but rarer than potei/poté/poterono.

irregularity.description: Modal verb alternating dev-/dobb- in the present, with the older variants debbo and debbono still admitted. The subjunctive is debba (also deva) and the future contracts to dovr-.

presente.english: I have to study for the exam.

passato_prossimo.italian: Ho dovuto lavorare fino a tardi.
passato_prossimo.english: I had to work until late.

imperfetto.english: I had to get up early every morning.

passato_remoto.english: He had to give up the trip.

futuro_semplice.english: You will have to decide soon.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't think he needs to worry.

condizionale_presente.english: You should rest more.

notes: Modal verb: directly followed by the infinitive, with no preposition.
The conditional 'dovrei / dovresti' is how Italian expresses English 'should'.
debbo / debbono / deva are standard but formal or literary; devo / devono / debba are the everyday choice.
Also means 'to owe' with a direct object: 'Ti devo dieci euro'.

irregularity.description: Modal verb with the palatal stem vogli- before -o and -ono, the diphthong vuo- in tu/lui, a double-r future (vorrò) and a strong passato remoto (volli, volle, vollero).

presente.english: I want to learn Italian.

imperfetto.english: I wanted to ask you a favour.

passato_remoto.english: He wanted to leave alone.

futuro_semplice.english: He will want to know everything.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't think he wants to come.

condizionale_presente.english: I would like a coffee, please.

notes: 'Vorrei' is the standard polite form when ordering or requesting; plain 'voglio' sounds blunt to strangers.
Modal verb: followed directly by the infinitive — 'voglio andare', never *'voglio di andare'.
With a noun it works as an ordinary transitive verb: 'Voglio un gelato'.
The imperative exists mainly in the formal written formula 'Vogliate…' (Please be so kind as to…).

verbs.english: to know (facts), to know how to

irregularity.description: Highly irregular present (so, sai, sa, sappiamo, sapete, sanno) with a subjunctive and imperative built on sappi-. The future contracts to sapr- and the passato remoto is strong (seppi, seppe, seppero).

presente.english: I can speak three languages.

passato_prossimo.english: I found out the news yesterday.

imperfetto.english: I didn't know you were here.

passato_remoto.english: He found out the truth too late.

futuro_semplice.english: Tomorrow we will know the result.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't think he can swim.

condizionale_presente.english: I wouldn't know what to say.

imperativo.english: Know that I am grateful to you.

notes: sapere = to know a fact or to know how to do something; conoscere = to be acquainted with a person or place.
In the passato prossimo it shifts meaning to 'to find out': 'Ho saputo che ti sposi'.
sapere + infinitive means 'to be able to' through learned skill: 'So guidare' (I can drive).
'Sa di…' means 'it tastes/smells of': 'Questo sa di limone'.

irregularity.description: Contracted infinitive from Latin bibere: the full stem bev- returns in nearly every form (bevo, bevevo, bevendo). The future has a double r (berrò) and the passato remoto is strong with -vv- (bevvi, bevve, bevvero).

presente.english: I drink a coffee every morning.

imperfetto.english: As a child I only drank milk.

passato_remoto.english: He drank it all in one go.

futuro_semplice.english: Tonight we will have a beer.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Voglio che tu beva più acqua.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I want you to drink more water.

condizionale_presente.english: I would gladly have a tea.

imperativo.english: Drink, it will do you good!

notes: Only the infinitive is short; every conjugated form is built on bev-.
Note the double r of the future and conditional: berrò, berrei — a very common spelling mistake.
The bevetti/bevette/bevettero series is admitted but far less common than bevvi/bevve/bevvero.

irregularity.description: Velar stem teng- before -o and -ono, diphthong ie- in tu/lui (tieni, tiene), double-r future (terrò) and strong passato remoto (tenni, tenne, tennero). The pattern is identical to venire.

presente.english: I keep the keys in my pocket.

passato_prossimo.italian: Ho tenuto il bambino in braccio.
passato_prossimo.english: I held the child in my arms.

imperfetto.english: He always kept the window open.

passato_remoto.english: He gave a memorable speech.

futuro_semplice.english: I will keep the documents.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Bisogna che tu tenga la calma.
congiuntivo_presente.english: You need to keep calm.

condizionale_presente.italian: Terrei la macchina ancora un anno.
condizionale_presente.english: I would keep the car another year.

notes: tenere a + noun/infinitive means 'to care about': 'Ci tengo molto'.
All derivatives follow the same pattern: mantenere, ottenere, contenere, appartenere, sostenere, trattenere.
'Tieni!' is the everyday way of handing something over, like English 'Here you go'.

irregularity.description: Velar stem rimang- before -o and -ono, double-r future (rimarrò), strong passato remoto (rimasi, rimase, rimasero) and the irregular participle rimasto.

presente.english: I'm staying home tonight.

passato_prossimo.italian: Siamo rimasti in ufficio fino a tardi.
passato_prossimo.english: We stayed at the office until late.

imperfetto.english: I always used to remain the last one.

passato_remoto.italian: Rimase in silenzio tutta la sera.
passato_remoto.english: He remained silent all evening.

futuro_semplice.english: I will stay here two more days.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I hope he stays with us.

condizionale_presente.english: I would stay, but I have to go.

notes: Takes essere: sono rimasto / sono rimasta / siamo rimasti / siamo rimaste.
Also means 'to be left over': 'Sono rimasti due biglietti'.
'Rimanere' + adjective describes a reaction: rimanere sorpreso, rimanere deluso.
permanere and the everyday synonym restare follow a regular -are pattern instead.

irregularity.description: The palatal gli becomes lg before -o and -ono (scelgo, scelgono), the passato remoto is strong (scelsi, scelse, scelsero) and the participle is scelto.

presente.italian: Scelgo sempre il menù del giorno.
presente.english: I always choose the menu of the day.

imperfetto.italian: Sceglieva sempre il posto vicino alla finestra.
imperfetto.english: He always used to choose the seat by the window.

passato_remoto.english: He chose to stay in Italy.

futuro_semplice.english: We will choose the present together.

congiuntivo_presente.english: It's better that he chooses.

condizionale_presente.english: I would choose the red one.

notes: The same gli → lg alternation appears in cogliere, togliere, sciogliere, raccogliere.
scegliere di + infinitive: 'Ho scelto di partire'.
The participle scelto is also used as an adjective meaning 'select, choice'.

irregularity.description: The present is regular; irregularity is concentrated in the strong passato remoto (vidi, vide, videro), the contracted future stem vedr- and the participle visto (with the regular veduto still admitted).

presente.english: I can't see well from a distance.

passato_prossimo.italian: Ieri ho visto un bel film.
passato_prossimo.english: Yesterday I saw a good film.

imperfetto.italian: Da qui si vedeva tutta la città.
imperfetto.english: From here you could see the whole city.

passato_remoto.italian: La vide per l'ultima volta nel 1970.
passato_remoto.english: He saw her for the last time in 1970.

futuro_semplice.english: We will see each other tomorrow.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Non credo che veda il problema.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't think he sees the problem.

condizionale_presente.english: I would gladly see that museum.

imperativo.english: See that you arrive on time!

notes: 'visto' is the everyday participle; 'veduto' is correct but literary.
'Ci vediamo!' is the standard way of saying 'See you!'.
provvedere and prevedere follow the pattern but keep regular participles: provveduto/provvisto, previsto.
vedere is also used impersonally: 'Si vede che…' = 'Clearly…'.

irregularity.description: Regular present, but a strong passato remoto (vissi, visse, vissero), a contracted future stem vivr- and the irregular participle vissuto.

presente.italian: Vivo a Milano da tre anni.
presente.english: I have been living in Milan for three years.

passato_prossimo.english: I lived abroad for two years.

imperfetto.english: We used to live in the countryside.

passato_remoto.english: He lived to be ninety.

futuro_semplice.english: We will live together from next year.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I think he still lives here.

condizionale_presente.english: I would happily live by the sea.

notes: Takes either auxiliary: 'Ho vissuto a Roma' and 'Sono vissuto a Roma' are both correct, avere being far more common in modern usage.
With a direct object only avere is possible: 'Ho vissuto un'esperienza incredibile'.
'Viva!' as an exclamation ('Long live…!') is the subjunctive form.
sopravvivere follows the same pattern and prefers essere.

verbs.english: to put, to place, to pose

irregularity.description: Contracted from Latin ponere: the stem pon- reappears everywhere (pongo, ponevo, ponendo), with a velar g before -o and -ono. Double-r future (porrò), strong passato remoto (posi, pose, posero) and participle posto.

presente.english: I am asking a simple question.

passato_prossimo.english: They put an end to the discussion.

imperfetto.italian: Poneva sempre molta attenzione ai dettagli.
imperfetto.english: He always paid great attention to detail.

passato_remoto.english: He laid the first stone in 1900.

futuro_semplice.english: We will raise the issue tomorrow.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Bisogna che si ponga il problema.
congiuntivo_presente.english: The problem needs to be raised.

condizionale_presente.italian: Porrei la domanda in modo diverso.
condizionale_presente.english: I would put the question differently.

imperativo.italian: Poni attenzione a quello che dici.
imperativo.english: Pay attention to what you say.

notes: Formal register: everyday Italian prefers mettere for the physical sense.
The whole family follows the same pattern: comporre, disporre, esporre, imporre, opporre, proporre, supporre.
Common set phrases: porre una domanda, porre fine a, porre attenzione.

verbs.english: to go up, to climb, to get on

irregularity.description: A velar g appears before -o and -ono (salgo, salgono) and throughout the singular subjunctive (salga); every other form is regular.

presente.english: I always walk up.

passato_prossimo.italian: Siamo saliti in cima alla torre.
passato_prossimo.english: We climbed to the top of the tower.

imperfetto.english: The price used to rise every year.

passato_remoto.english: He got on the train at the last moment.

futuro_semplice.english: We will go up by lift.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Temo che il prezzo salga ancora.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I fear the price will rise further.

condizionale_presente.english: I would go up, but I'm afraid of heights.

notes: essere when intransitive ('Sono salito sull'autobus'), avere with a direct object ('Ho salito le scale').
Also used for prices and temperature going up.
Its opposite scendere is irregular in a different way: scesi, sceso.

irregularity.description: The stressed stem takes the diphthong uo (muoio, muori, muore, muoiono) while noi and voi keep mor-. The participle is the irregular morto.

presente.english: I'm starving!

passato_prossimo.italian: Il suo cane è morto l'anno scorso.

imperfetto.english: He was dying of fear.

passato_remoto.english: He died in 1912.

futuro_semplice.english: These plants will die without water.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't want it to die like this.

condizionale_presente.english: I'd die for an ice cream right now.

imperativo.english: Don't die of boredom, go out!

notes: Takes essere: è morto / è morta / sono morti / sono morte.
The archaic future morrò and conditional morrei are found in poetry; modern Italian uses morirò and morirei.
Very common hyperbolically: morire di fame, morire di sonno, morire dal ridere.

irregularity.description: The present is regular apart from the spelling of the soft/hard c; the passato remoto is strong with -cqu- (nacqui, nacque, nacquero) and the participle is nato.

presente.english: New ideas are born every day.

imperfetto.italian: In quegli anni nascevano molte imprese.
imperfetto.english: In those years many companies were being founded.

passato_remoto.english: He was born in 1895.

futuro_semplice.english: The baby will be born in May.

congiuntivo_presente.english: I hope he is born healthy.

condizionale_presente.italian: Da quell'idea nascerebbe un bel progetto.
condizionale_presente.english: A fine project would come out of that idea.

notes: Takes essere: sono nato / sono nata.
Unlike English, Italian uses the passato prossimo for one's own birth: 'Sono nato nel 1990'.
Figuratively used for ideas, projects and rivers: 'Il fiume nasce dalle Alpi'.
The related conoscere shares the -cqu- passato remoto pattern (conobbi, conobbe, conobbero).

irregularity.description: The stem doubles the c before -o, -io and -iono (piaccio, piacciono) and throughout the subjunctive (piaccia). The passato remoto is strong with -cqu- (piacqui, piacque, piacquero).

presente.english: I like Italian music.

passato_prossimo.italian: Ci è piaciuto molto il film.

imperfetto.italian: Da bambino mi piacevano i fumetti.
imperfetto.english: As a child I liked comics.

passato_remoto.english: Everyone liked that book.

futuro_semplice.english: You will like this place.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Non credo che gli piaccia il pesce.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I don't think he likes fish.

condizionale_presente.english: I would like to visit Naples.

notes: The English subject becomes the Italian indirect object: 'I like pizza' = 'Mi piace la pizza' (literally: pizza pleases me).
The verb agrees with the thing liked: mi piace il libro / mi piacciono i libri.
Takes essere, so the participle agrees with the thing liked: 'Mi è piaciuta la casa', 'Mi sono piaciuti i film'.
The same construction governs mancare, servire, bastare, restare, interessare and dispiacere.

irregularity.description: Contracted from Latin traducere: the stem traduc- returns in every conjugated form (traduco, traducevo, traducendo). The passato remoto is strong with -ss- (tradussi, tradusse, tradussero) and the participle is tradotto.

presente.english: I translate articles from English.

imperfetto.italian: Traduceva libri per una casa editrice.
imperfetto.english: She used to translate books for a publisher.

passato_remoto.italian: Tradusse la Divina Commedia in inglese.
passato_remoto.english: He translated the Divine Comedy into English.

futuro_semplice.english: I will translate the text by Friday.

congiuntivo_presente.italian: Voglio che tu traduca questa frase.
congiuntivo_presente.english: I want you to translate this sentence.

condizionale_presente.english: I would translate this title differently.

notes: The whole -durre family behaves identically: condurre, produrre, ridurre, introdurre, sedurre, dedurre.
Note the double r in the future and conditional: tradurrò, tradurrei.
tradurre da … a / in: 'tradurre dall'italiano all'inglese'.
